_comment: The SCA dependency audit, driven by the faked network below, reading the committed package-lock.json alone. tiny-obscure-helper is a package the lock marks as declared, and nobody uses it (12 downloads a month), so unpopular-source-dependency rejects it, anchored at its lock entry: a dependency the reviewer cannot lean on the community for must be shipped readable instead. vitest (a devDependency) and platform-binary (an optionalDependency) are declared too, so they are popularity-gated the same way, though this fixture does not exercise that: the network map answers a downloads lookup for tiny-obscure-helper only, so theirs 404 and record nothing. Every installed package is OSV-audited in one batch, and the batch answers each of the three with a MODERATE advisory - which produces NOTHING: a source review reports a package when it fails the review, not when it merely appears, and that absence is the threshold's end-to-end pin for declared dependencies. The batch results pair by position with the `queries` it names, one per package the lock installs.
